summary: High-level POC scoping focused on throughput acceptance test and integrating QuantaHealth's custom load scripts. Discussed streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, expected traffic profile, success criteria, and a short timeline for a 2-week benchmark run. Agreement to exchange artifacts and run an initial integration next week.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-17 15:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (RD Solutions), Markus (QuantaHealth Head of ML), Priya (Platform Eng), Daniel (PM)

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, i know it's the week before holidays so we appreciate the time. quick round robin?
[00:12] Markus: yeah thanks, Markus here. goal is to validate throughput and make sure any integration we do fits our current harness. primary success for us is a p99 under the SLO and no regression in generation quality.
[00:30] Priya: hi, this is Priya, i'll be running the scripts and container side. we have an internal harness that spins multiple runners, it supports streaming edges but we typically run non-streaming for nightly jobs.
[00:45] Ethan: cool, Ethan from Redwood. today we'll sketch the benchmark matrix and how we adapt to your runner. quick question — what's your typical payload size and sequence lengths?
[00:58] Daniel: most prompts are ~120 tokens average, some system prompts push to 400 tokens, and about 20% of calls are streaming-friendly (chat with partial replies).
[01:12] Samira: good, that helps. for success criteria do you have explicit latency numbers? p95/p99 targets?
[01:20] Markus: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 350ms is our goal for interactive endpoints. for batch jobs throughput is more important — we want to sustain ~150 rps for concurrent inference on our peak pods.
[01:34] Ethan: okay makes sense. tradeoffs we'll need to call out: streaming tends to improve median latency for first byte but complicates batching and reduces effective throughput per GPU. non-streaming easier to batch and gives better token throughput.
[01:48] Priya: we were hoping to test both modes — at least a few runs streaming enabled, a few non-streaming. our harness can toggle a flag — but the adapter needs to signal stream vs non-stream per client.
[02:02] Lena: we can add that flag to the runner adapter. Ethan and I will look at your runner API. can you share the script entrypoint and a sample Dockerfile?
[02:12] Priya: yes, i'll upload those after this call. note: our runner has a per-request retry policy and client-side batching that may interfere with Redwood's batching, so we'll need to coordinate TTLs.
[02:25] Samira: great flag — we should align on batch window and max latency budget. typical Redwood config param names we'll propose in the matrix — e.g., batch_max_items, batch_max_latency_ms.
[02:38] Markus: also curious about model variants and quantization. we plan to try a 4-bit quantized variant for cost testing, but we need to ensure quality checks pass.
[02:49] Ethan: yes — we'll include two model configs: baseline FP16 or full-precision, and a quantized candidate. we'll run A/B comparisons on a fixed eval set you provide. quality gates will include ROUGE/EM/perplexity-ish equivalents and a small manual spot-check.
[03:07] Daniel: how do you suggest we capture quality regressions automatically?
[03:13] Lena: we can wire the evaluation harness to compute per-prompt score distributions and fail the run if overall quality drops more than X% vs baseline. propose threshold of < 3% relative quality drop as initial gate.
[03:28] Markus: sounds reasonable. on telemetry, we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency. retention for logs must be 90 days for audits.
[03:40] Samira: Redwood can export per-route traces and token counts; we'll add a short doc on retention and SSO access for your audit team.
[03:50] Priya: one operational note — our network egress is limited, so we'd prefer to run the benchmark on a Dedicated pool or private VPC. is that something Redwood supports for a POC?
[04:03] Ethan: yes, for POCs we can stand up a small dedicated pool in your VPC or run the tests in Redwood Dedicated while using an IP allowlist. we'll include both options in the plan. differences will be noted in the matrix (latency delta expected between on-prem and hosted).
[04:20] Samira: timeline suggestion: send benchmark matrix + config flags by Friday (12/19), Quanta shares scripts + sample prompts by 12/20, then we schedule a 2-hour integration run (focused smoke test) week of 12/22, followed by a 4-10 day ramped benchmark run to gather p95/p99 across variants.
[04:38] Daniel: 4-10 day range okay; we prefer the shorter end if we can get meaningful stats.
[04:45] Ethan: for harness specifics — do you run async clients or sync? this affects how we shape the load.
[04:52] Priya: async. we have an event loop that drives N workers and collects partial streams.
[04:58] Ethan: then we'll adapt the runner adapter to provide both streaming and chunked non-streaming endpoints. you'll need to pass an environment variable to toggle behavior in the adapter.
[05:08] Markus: what about warm KV cache behavior? our real traffic has high prefix duplication, so a run without cache will understate performance.
[05:18] Lena: good point. we'll add a cache-warmed run and a cold-cache run in the matrix. we'll also instrument hit-rate to compare to production-like hit-rate you provide.
[05:29] Samira: perfect. logging — please mark any IVs where you want PII redaction; we'll redact logs before storing.
[05:37] Priya: yes we'll annotate.
[05:41] Samira: ok quick recap of acceptance criteria we wrote down: p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 350ms for interactive; sustain 150 rps for throughput tests in non-streaming; quality drop < 3% vs baseline on your eval set; two model configs (baseline + quantized candidate); pass both cold and warm cache runs.
[05:59] Markus: yep that's the core. also want to capture cost per 1M tokens as a back-of-envelope for procurement.
[06:07] Ethan: we'll include token-cost estimates for each model/config and run.
[06:11] Daniel: ok next steps for us — we'll share the sample prompts, runner script, and Dockerfile today or tomorrow.
[06:18] Samira: and we'll send the benchmark matrix and a sample Redwood adapter in a repo link — and propose the integration window.
[06:27] Priya: one more question: if streaming runs are noisy for variance, do you recommend more replicas or longer runs?
[06:34] Lena: longer runs for variance smoothing; replicas help but if variance is network-driven the replicas won't help. we'll call out confidence intervals in the report.
[06:44] Samira: great. any blockers?
[06:47] Markus: none immediate. procurement and security will want a quick security questionnaire; can you share SOC2 attestation?
[06:54] Samira: yes i'll attach SOC2 + security pack in the follow-up.
[06:58] Daniel: thanks everyone.
[07:00] Samira: thanks — we'll sync in the follow-up email with dates and links.

References/links mentioned: 1) draft benchmark matrix (will be shared) 2) sample adapter repo: https://redwood-docs/samples/quanta-adapter-repo 3) customer benchmark plan placeholder: https://redwood-docs/samples/quanta-benchmark-plan.xlsx

Notes on transcription: some speaker tags may be approximate and certain technical terms were auto-corrected (eg. KV cache, batch windows).
